newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour to launch business manifesto in Feb.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour to launch business manifesto in Feb.

text.p: The UK opposition Labour Party is to launch a business manifesto in February containing five key goals which would guide the party in government, finance spokesman Gordon Brown said on Friday.
In a speech to businessmen in London, Brown said stability and low inflation and tough rules on public expenditure and borrowing were among the goals.
The remainder were high levels and improved quality of investment, a new skills revolution to boost productivity and constructive engagement with Britain's European partners.
"The content of this manifesto will be the most important signal yet that on the central issues of the '90s, new Labour and the business community are as one," Brown said.
The business vote has traditionally been bagged by the ruling Conservative party, but an all-out bid by Labour to woo Britain's big bosses recently has begun to erode that position.

"Never again should we return to the situation here in Britain...where one party is seen as pro-business and the other is seen as anti-business," said Brown. "We can and will work together to meet common concerns."
Brown added that at the end of February Labour would hold a business summit.
